summary.oneLiner: Asset-light, debt-free branded-TMT franchise model where royalty income (now INR175 cr, +25% YoY on per-ton rate hikes) is becoming the dominant earnings driver — PBT +31% to INR106 cr despite flat-ish topline, with a clean balance sheet and ~INR300 cr treasury yet to be deployed.

one-line thesis: Asset-light, debt-free branded-TMT franchise model where royalty income (now INR175 cr, +25% YoY on per-ton rate hikes) is becoming the dominant earnings driver — PBT +31% to INR106 cr despite flat-ish topline, with a clean balance sheet and ~INR300 cr treasury yet to be deployed.
financial scorecard:
**Q4 FY26 (vs Q4 FY25):**
- Franchisee steel volume: 10.2 lakh MT vs 9.4 lakh MT, **+8% YoY**
- Own-mfg steel volume: 31,624 MT vs 31,950 MT, **flat YoY** (plant ~100% utilized)
- Royalty income (franchisee): **INR46 cr vs INR38 cr, +19% YoY**
- Total revenue: INR208 cr vs INR198 cr, **+5% YoY**
- PBT: INR24 cr, **+8% YoY**; PBT margin 11.7%
- PAT: INR17 cr, **+2% YoY**

**FY26 (vs FY25):**
- Franchisee volume: **37.9 lakh MT vs 34.4 lakh MT, +10% YoY**; total sales volume cited at 39 lakh MT
- Own-mfg volume: 121,092 MT vs 119,841 MT, **flat YoY**
- Royalty income: **INR175 cr vs INR139 cr, +25% YoY** (volume +10% + royalty rate hike)
- Royalty realization: **INR435/MT vs INR398/MT (FY25) vs ~INR380 earlier** — ~+10% rate hike
- Total revenue: **INR763 cr vs INR747 cr, +2% YoY** (topline muted by softer TMT selling prices)
- PBT: **INR106 cr vs INR80 cr, +31% YoY**; PBT margin 13.8%
- PAT: **INR78 cr vs INR61 cr, +29% YoY**
- ROCE 26.8%, ROE 19.8%; **debt-free** as of 31-Mar-2026
- Cash/treasury: **~INR300 cr** on balance sheet (deployment policy being framed)
- **One-offs:** INR20 cr opportunistic equity investment in paints business (Mar-2026), ~4% stake — not recurring.
- ASP for TMT bars marginally softer YoY (broader steel pricing); franchise model insulates margins as royalty is fixed per-ton (not %).
guidance (critical):
- **Royalty rate:** plan to raise **10–15% every year**, layered on ~10% annual volume growth (run-rate of last 2–3 years).
- **Volume:** ~10% p.a. franchisee volume growth expected to continue.
- **Royalty mix:** expect royalty to be an "increasingly larger proportion" of earnings over coming years — the defining financial characteristic.
- **Own mfg:** single plant (1.25 lakh MT, Delhi/NCR), 100% utilized, to stay 100% near term; topline swings only with steel price; no capacity-add guided.
- **Network:** focus on growing volume of existing ~100 units (50 TMT + 50 structural/pipe/colour-coated), NOT adding units broadly — except South India where new franchisees are planned.
- No explicit consolidated margin guidance; bottom line driven mainly by royalty income, insulated from steel price swings.
order book & pipeline (n/a — franchise r:
- **>12,500 dealers** across India (one of the most extensive branded-steel networks); "can supply X quantity in 24 hours, no one can at shorter notice."
- ~100 manufacturing franchise units (50 TMT bar + 50 structural/pipe/colour-coated). Net unit count flat YoY (~4–5 units left, ~4–5 added).
- Franchisee capacity ~4–5 million MT (data being recompiled, to be released in Q1); FY26 volume 39 lakh MT against it.
- Regional volume mix: North 31%, East 35%, West 19%, South 15% — South is the under-penetrated growth focus.
- Estimated **~20% retail branded TMT market share** (management estimate).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Own manufacturing (re-rolling):** 1 plant, Delhi/NCR, 1.25 lakh MT, 100% utilized; price-pass-through so price moves hit topline but not bottom line much.
- **Franchise/branded:** royalty charged per-ton (not %), so insulated from steel price; the profit engine. FY26 royalty INR175 cr.
- Products beyond TMT (via franchisees): structural steel, pipes, colour-coated sheets.
growth verticals / optionality:
- Royalty rate escalation (10–15%/yr) — primary lever.
- South India geographic expansion (new franchisees).
- Capacity expansion within existing franchise units.
- Brand extension across structural/pipe/colour-coated lines.
- Treasury (~INR300 cr) optionality — policy pending; mgmt says it will fund steel business + shareholder rewards (not paints).
- Structural tailwind: shift unorganized → organized/branded steel; Kamdhenu commands brand premium of ~INR1,500–6,000/ton (avg ~INR2,600/ton).
margins & cost dynamics:
- FY26 PBT margin 13.8% (vs implied lower FY25); Q4 11.7%.
- Royalty per-ton model decouples profitability from steel-price cyclicality — key margin protection.
- Raw material: domestic iron ore firm/up-trending; global iron ore stable; crude/natural gas volatile (geopolitics). Near-term margin pressure flagged for both company and franchisees, but franchise model distributes input-cost risk to partners.
- ASP for TMT marginally softer YoY; mgmt prioritized volume/penetration over price.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- No major own-capex guided; own plant already at 100% utilization with no expansion announced.
- Growth is capex-light (franchise/royalty model) — limited slippage risk; capacity additions occur on franchisee balance sheets, not Kamdhenu's.
capital allocation:
- **Dividend: INR0.40/share (40% of INR1 face value)** declared for FY26.
- Debt-free; ROCE 26.8%, ROE 19.8%.
- ~INR300 cr treasury — formal treasury/shareholder-reward policy being framed (watch for buyback/special dividend).
- INR20 cr (~4% stake) opportunistic investment in demerged paints business at depressed share price; explicitly a one-time, no further infusion; treasury to serve steel + shareholders only.
risks & watch-items:
- Steel-price/raw-material volatility (iron ore up, crude/gas volatile) pressuring own-mfg and franchisee margins near-term.
- Topline optically flat (+2%) as selling prices soften — masks royalty-led profit growth.
- Franchise quality control / brand dilution risk as network scales.
- Competition: national (Tata, Jindal) and strong regional brands.
- Treasury deployment uncertainty (~INR300 cr idle; policy pending) — capital-allocation execution risk.
- Capacity data not yet recompiled (to be released Q1) — disclosure lag.
management quality / tone: - Confident, focused, candid (CFO openly admits stale capacity data, lays out per-ton royalty economics and regional mix). Clear capital-allocation discipline emphasis (no paints scaling, treasury for steel + shareholders). Strong conviction in brand premium and asset-light durability. Tone: measured optimism, structural-growth framing tied to govt infra capex.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The real story is **price (royalty rate), not just volume**: 25% royalty growth on 10% volume = rate-driven margin engine that can compound at 10–15%/yr regardless of steel cycle.
- Topline is a misleading KPI here — it carries steel-price pass-through from own mfg; royalty + PBT are the true value metrics.
- ~INR300 cr cash + debt-free + 27% ROCE on an asset-light base = potential for outsized shareholder returns once treasury policy lands.
- Deliberately NOT chasing new franchise units (except South) — prioritizing per-unit volume/capacity over network sprawl, protecting brand quality.
- Royalty is per-ton (not ad valorem), so a steel-price crash does not hit Kamdhenu's economics — a genuine cyclicality hedge.

| Shift unorganized → organized/branded TMT | Kamdhenu — KAMDHENU · 532741 · Branded TMT | Unorganized/local TMT makers | Branded players capture premium (~INR2,600/ton) as consumers move to brands ✅ |
| Govt INR12.2 lakh cr infra capex / housing push | Kamdhenu — KAMDHENU · 532741 · Branded TMT; broader TMT makers (Tata Steel, JSW, Jindal) | — | TMT is foundational input for all infra/residential; broad-based demand ⭐ |

Debt-free, ROCE 26.8% / ROE 19.8%, ~INR300 cr treasury (deployment policy pending). Dividend INR0.40/sh (40%). themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Deck claims "WE ARE THE Largest Branded TMT BAR Player in India", with brand sales turnover of "Rs. 23,000^ Crores" (^ As on FY 26) and "Volume Sold (FY26) 39 Lakh MT".
- Distribution moat described as a decentralised pan-India network: "100+ Franchisees", "12,500+ Dealers", "500+ Distributors", with each franchisee, distributor and dealer assigned an exclusive designated geographical area.
- In 2016 the name changed from Kamdhenu Ispat Ltd. to Kamdhenu Ltd., "positioned as branding and marketing company"; the franchisee association model was innovated in 2004 and the company "Became largest TMT selling brand in India" in 2015.
- Deck emphasises heavy brand investment as the moat: print/TV/outdoor/digital campaigns, dealer and customer meets, and a long roster of celebrity endorsers; awards cited include "The Extraordinaire –Brand: Most Trusted Brand - Infrastructure & Building Materials" (2025-26).

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Demerger] The paint business was separated under a Scheme of Arrangement: board approval in 2020, filing with NCLT Chandigarh Bench in 2021, NCLT approval in 2022, and listing of Kamdhenu Ventures Limited (Paint Business) equity shares on NSE and BSE on 24th January 2023 — so the deck's brand and volume figures relate to the post-demerger steel entity.
- [Cost shock] The deck flags a war-driven cost impact: Q1 FY27 PBT "included an additional ~₹1.76 crore of legal expenses and ~₹3 crore of fuel costs due to the impact of West Asia war", with fuel prices "subsequently normalizing".
- [Group vs entity] Brand sales turnover of ~₹23,000 crore is franchisee/brand-level throughput, not the listed company's revenue — Kamdhenu Limited's own reported revenue from operations is a small fraction of it (₹213.3 Cr in Q1 FY27), with royalty on franchisee sales the key monetisation line.
